messages.subject: from_to for repeated simulation
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to using simmer for DES (coming from the world of Simul8). This is a great tool and thanks for all the hard work you've put in. I normally use these programs for healthcare simulation and have a question about simulating different patient arrival times throughout the day.

Is there currently a way to run a simulation for (as an example) 5 days, where patients would arrive at different rates between 3 different periods in the day. Such as

1 patient every 10 mins from 8am to 4pm
1 patient every 30 mins from 4pm to 12am
1 patient every 60 mins from 12am to 8am

I got the general idea to work fine using the code below (defining different patient types, though if there is a simpler way to do this, then I'm happy to take on suggestions), but then if I wanted to simulate this over 5 days, is there a way to reset the clock at minute 1440 (midnight) on day one, so that I don't need to define 15 different groups of patients?

Thanks

simmer() %>%

    ...

    add_generator("patient_on_", patient_traj, from_to(0, 8*24, function() rexp(1, rate = 1/60), arrive = F), mon = 2) %>%
    add_generator("patient_am_", patient_traj, from_to(8*24, 16*60, function() rexp(1, rate = 1/15), arrive = F), mon = 2) %>%
    add_generator("patient_pm_", patient_traj, from_to(16*60, 24*60, function() rexp(1, rate = 1/15), arrive = F), mon = 2) %>%

    run(60*24*5)

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] from_to for repeated simulation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Try this one:
from_to <- function(start_time, stop_time, dist, arrive=TRUE, every=NULL) {
  stopifnot(is.null(every) || every >= stop_time)
  started <- FALSE
  init <- 0
  counter <- 0
  function() {
    while (TRUE){
      if (!started) {
        started <<- TRUE
        if (arrive) {
          dt <- start_time - init
        } else {
          dt <- dist()
          dt[1] <- dt[1] + start_time - init
        }
      } else {
        dt <- dist()
      }
      len <- length(dt)
      dt <- dt[cumsum(dt) + counter < stop_time]
      counter <<- counter + sum(dt)
      if (len == length(dt))
        return(dt)
      if (is.null(every))
        return(c(dt, -1))
      if (length(dt))
        return(dt)
      start_time <<- start_time + every
      stop_time <<- stop_time + every
      started <<- FALSE
      init <<- counter
    }
  }
}

with every=24*60. If it works correctly, we can update this convenience function and it will be available in the next release.

Regards,
Iñaki
​
